sonnet.problem: Card 1 says the Day of the LORD is near and coming quickly. Card 2 then asks what the nation should gather before, and its right answer is the Day of the LORD's anger. The setup line gives the answer away.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The fill-in-the-blank question repeats the fact card 16 just asked and revealed: that the remnant lies down among the houses of Ashkelon. Card 17 is also on the same verse and re-uses that answer.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: "Every one of those gods is about to find out" adds a timing ("about to") that the text doesn't give for this prediction.
sonnet.rule: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added. A prediction stays a prediction

sonnet.problem: The card says the city "is a resting place for beasts" as a present fact. It is part of a prediction that Nineveh will be made a desolation, and it should be told as one.
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls." What a prophet sees in a vision can be told as what he sees.
